title: ext2 invalidation error may bypass write rollback
mechanism: InodeInner::write_direct_at calls prepare_write (which may grow the page cache and allocate blocks) and then invalidate_range with ?, so an invalidation writeback error returns without rollback_write when the write extends past EOF.
contract: A failed write leaves no page-cache growth or block allocation past the unchanged file size (InodeInner::prepare_write rollback rule, Linux ext2_write_failed).
observed: Source only: an invalidate_range error in the direct-write path returns before rollback_write, which can leave allocated blocks and page-cache capacity past EOF.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes an O_DIRECT write spanning old EOF with injected writeback failure, checking st_blocks and e2fsck.

caveats: Static coverage only. Needs writeback-failure injection to trigger. Draft PR #3297 covers it by inspection but is unmerged. Report CR-2 is this entry, brief CR-2 is AST-33/34.
